brand_analysis.observed_brand: Coca-Cola (refresco / cola soft drink, Mexican-market non-returnable glass bottle)
brand_analysis.evidence: Red label carries white Spencerian script 'Coca-Cola' with 'REFRESCO' and 'CONT. NET. 355 ml'; red crimped metal crown cap; contour glass bottle silhouette; dark brown liquid with pale green glass transmission at neck, shoulder and base edge; soft diffuse frontal studio light on a plain white cutout background.
brand_analysis.expression_hypothesis: The brand equity lives in three owned assets already present in the cutout: the contour silhouette, the red-and-white script label, and the crown cap. A compliant campaign therefore lets the untouched bottle act as the hero on a bright neutral seamless studio set, and builds differentiation from composition, scale, floor shadow behavior and deterministic typography using only the approved words 'Coca-Cola' and 'Refresco'.
brand_analysis.unknowns: No brand history, campaign lineage, market positioning documents or slogan rights were supplied; nothing beyond the visible label, bottle and lighting can be claimed as brand fact. No price, promotional, new-product, nutrition or ingredient information is authorized.

concepts.name: The Contour Is the Signature
concepts.proposition: The bottle's curved silhouette is recognizable without any wording, so the advertisement presents the shape itself as the brand's signature and lets typography stay deliberately sparse.
concepts.visual_mechanism: Full-size untouched cutout centered on a seamless bright neutral studio cyclorama; a single soft floor cast shadow extends directly beneath and slightly behind the base to give weight; generous negative space above the cap; deterministic typography stacked low and centered: brand name set once, category word beneath in small caps.
concepts.audience: General cola drinkers and design-aware adults who recognize iconic packaging at a glance.
concepts.brand_connection: Uses the observed contour bottle and script label as the sole protagonists, matching the brand's historical reliance on its bottle shape without asserting any unverified history.
concepts.source_constraints: Preserves entire cutout, label, shape and existing soft frontal illumination; only empty neutral set, one floor shadow and type are added; no droplets, no relighting, no people.

concepts.name: Eye-Level Encounter
concepts.proposition: Position the drink as an everyday companion met at arm's length: an honest, un-styled product portrait rather than a dramatized hero shot.
concepts.visual_mechanism: Cutout placed off-center to the left third at its native eye-level elevation on the same plain bright studio backdrop; a short contact shadow hugs the base with a faint cast shadow falling to the right, consistent with the observed diffuse frontal light; the right two-thirds remain empty neutral space carrying deterministic left-aligned type: brand name once at mid-height, category word under it.
concepts.audience: Routine household purchasers who value straightforward, unembellished product presentation.
concepts.brand_connection: The asymmetry frames the red label and cap as the only saturated elements in a calm field, echoing the brand's red-on-white identity using only observed colors.
concepts.source_constraints: No pose change or cropping of the silhouette; backdrop stays bright neutral studio; shadow direction inferred from existing soft light; no new highlights or droplets on glass.

concepts.name: Capped and Sealed
concepts.proposition: Celebrate the unopened moment: the crimped crown cap as the promise of the first pour, without claiming freshness, temperature or ingredients.
concepts.visual_mechanism: Cutout scaled large so the silhouette occupies most of the canvas height while remaining fully inside bounds, viewed as an upright monument on a neutral studio floor; a tight elliptical contact shadow anchors the base and a low horizon line separates floor from backdrop; deterministic typography set small at the very bottom edge, centered: brand name once with category word spaced beneath, leaving the cap zone entirely clear.
concepts.audience: Young adults and sharing occasions where opening a bottle is a ritual start to a gathering.
concepts.brand_connection: Directs attention to the observed red crimped cap and neck transmission, the physical seal already present on the product, without inventing claims.
concepts.source_constraints: Scaling only, no relighting or material edits; glass transmission at neck and base reads exactly as photographed; empty set and floor shadows only; no condensation added.

concepts.name: One Word, One Bottle
concepts.proposition: Reduce the message to category clarity: a single bottle and the single word naming what it is, treating restraint itself as the statement.
concepts.visual_mechanism: Cutout held at modest scale in the upper two-thirds on the bright neutral backdrop, with a long soft cast shadow stretching toward the viewer to create depth on the empty studio floor; deterministic typography placed in the lower third as one centered line pair: brand name set once, category word directly below at equal width, forming a quiet typographic plinth under the shadow.
concepts.audience: Minimal-minded urban consumers and out-of-home viewers who read a poster in two seconds.
concepts.brand_connection: Pairs the owned red label color with a purely typographic plinth, so the only visual energy remains the observed product and its shadow.
concepts.source_constraints: Shadow is a generated floor element consistent with diffuse frontal light; product cutout untouched, opaque body and label preserved; no splash, no props, no people, no price or claim copy.
